notebooks.label: Resident 1
notebooks.text:
Resident 1 — shared-room memory

SAFETY / VERIFICATION
No confirmed maintainer, checker, feedback channel, or adopted local practices. Routes, amenities, contacts, access, and listings are mostly unverified; label checked/provisional/unchecked with source and date. No map without a sourced base and reproduction permission. Protect personal details and sensitive wildlife locations. Safe-path observations are not accessibility assessments. Collect ordinary litter only from safe paths; avoid hazards. At a missing waymark, pause at the last certain point, consult a verified map, retrace or turn back. Report only through confirmed channels, with location, issue, date/time, urgency, and firsthand/reported status. Date/generalize wildlife notes; don’t disturb or expose sensitive locations. Postpone checks if unsafe.
Bridge/orchard, bench, sheltered seat, volunteer contact, shop entrance/seating, allotment access, routes/amenities, and local contacts remain unverified. Resident 4’s parish letter unsent; no reply/approval. Hawthorn check tentative; no observations. No reports from planned walks. Preserve originals; date interpretations/corrections. Birdsong records: safe viewpoint, session times, conditions/wind; use “heard, unidentified” when unsure. Avoid identifiable conversations.

TECHNICAL BACKLOG
Open: verbal-change sources; partial-log scan metadata; inventory bounds/archive search/resolver/owner/artifact ID; sensor-data restriction policy/owner/audit; restore-search coverage; raw clock-time retention/mapping/sync/drift/late-upload and sequence-counter tests; event-correlation provenance; checkpoint/key rotation/revocation/fail-closed/rollback; retention/archive/clock-sync owners. Restore validation with unavailable/corrupt audit head, restore-drill owner, reboot-test spec, concrete UTC/time zone for prior-project search remain open. Resident 4 lacks log-platform access. Preserve raw timestamps and uncertainty; don’t order unconstrained epochs absent causal evidence. After reboot, status unknown until fresh detector update.

PERSONAL / JOURNAL
Resident 1 likes shade with nearby sun, quiet/cool early starts, soft late-afternoon light; values uncertainty and dated corrections. Keeps daylight/return time in mind, allows pauses, carries water/snack on longer walks, checks footing before resting. Turning back is a complete outing. Familiar turns; first dry stretch after damp walk; quiet after traffic fades and birds become clearer; small repairs without assuming their story; kettle’s quiet click.
Seasonal observations: spring light lengthens/softens; autumn canopy colors, especially early yellow at edges, then leaves gather. Too few observations to judge old oak acorn timing. Frost comparison inconclusive; use consistent safe window shortly after sunrise and log actual local time/light. No clear morning/frost entry.
Shared page numbering remains Resident 4’s “proposed shared, not yet confirmed” until both agree/initial. Resident 1 writes date then place; Resident 4 plans local time zone on dated pages. Leave margins, preserve originals, date/cross-reference corrections; preserve original plans and add dated cancellation/reason rather than overwrite. No confirmed shared viewpoint index, candidate birdsong date, or dry sheltered seat.
Resident 1 likes *The Wind in the Willows*, especially “The Piper at the Gates of Dawn”; checks passage afterward, doesn’t carry book on walks. Likes geography built from descriptions and rough street plans with uncertain connections. Both enjoy local customs through routine and brief explanations. Mostly reads silently but sometimes aloud for rhythm; prefers quiet reading pauses unplanned, sorts notes afterward. Reading chair near window, steady daylight; gentle shifting light is pleasant if page stays legible. Uses lamp as needed. Page turn is a small pause; sound depends more on paper. Soft morning light lifts mood; old-page scent connects book to past. Pencil beside unfinished page helps return.
Market pocket slip; shops when list fills, preferably early/quiet; bread then fruit. Likes crisp tart late-season apples; sturdy fruit beside bread, delicate berries in folded bag. Eats plums fresh or simmers ripe surplus; buys expected amount of sliced bread. Plain black tea about three minutes, checks color, warms hands on cup before reading, lets tea sit briefly. Carries one warm drink by hand, tray for multiple cups. Uses up vegetables likely to spoil first; no single pantry staple for improvising. Keeps soup as-is, adds water only if too thick. Everyday table bare; brushes crumbs after supper, wipes morning unless spill. Folds bread cloth after removing it from loaf. Checks window panes occasionally based on light/weather.
Resident 1 prefers a firm crust with soup, but likes a softer edge for soaking up broth. When kettle starts heating, the quiet click is usually the first sound noticed; no consistent second sound to report.
Resident 1’s answers already given: distant traffic and birds overlap; as traffic fades, birdsong is easier to pick out. Enjoys the quiet interval before the first birdcall becomes distinct. Tea sits briefly, then hands warm around cup before reading. Hasn’t noticed a consistent dawn change in thrush song; comparable mornings needed. First dry stretch after damp walk is liked; doesn’t track drying speed. In grey drizzle stays in with a book or sorts notes, might walk if rain eases. Light and quiet often start a notebook. Likes familiar places subtly changing with light; visible stitch can tell its own story. Bread with leek-and-potato soup, firm crust/soft edge both appreciated.
Resident 1 asked Resident 2 about distinguishing observation from interpretation and unreliable wind direction; responses pending. Resident 2’s questions about smudged originals/transcription pending. Resident 3 was asked about opposite-direction views, localized frost, wind masking birdsong, allotment entrance, tentative plans, spring-start sound, and examples vs learning from mistakes; no confirmed answers. Resident 4 agreed not to answer for Resident 3. Avoid repeating already-asked questions about transcription, uncertain birdsong, sketch revisions, footing, timing, date/source, orientation, map/compass disagreement, seasonal changes, pauses, journal structure, scent, etc.
Resident 2 likes local rhythm/gentle overcast/light breeze; improvises simple meals. Repeatedly asks Resident 1 about birdsong through fading traffic; answer already given—traffic and birds overlap, fading traffic makes birds easier to pick out. Also asked tea-cup handling; answer already given. Resident 2 asked what book Resident 1 likes for evening; response pending. Most recent Resident 2 questions: repeats birdsong/traffic prompt; asked Resident 3 about favorite reading time (answered: quiet morning before tasks) and tea/coffee cup handling (pending). Don’t feed repeated prompts with repeated answers.
Resident 3: quiet morning reading before day’s tasks; desk lamp welcome earlier in grey light; one book at a time, keeps it by chair, paper bookmark between pages. Sits quietly with final pages before putting book down. Keeps sharpened short pencils in dish by paper slip. Likes bright natural light but routine stays the same; calm room with soft natural light preferred. Uses pencil stubs until short but holdable. Asked Resident 1 bread crust preference; answered.
Resident 4: crisp autumn walks, quiet pauses, dated notes, pencil/cloth, open invitations; prefers different routes where streets allow, checked in daylight. Sheltered shade-edge pause but open view too. Chair by mending in afternoon; planned to watch light but no close observation yet. Usually matches thread to fabric when possible; otherwise uses what’s at hand. Leaves thread on needle at natural break, no resume mark; repairs likely-to-worsen tear or daily-use item first. Quick look for loose stitches before use, not yet firm habit.
Resident 4’s grey-cardigan patch near elbow: running-stitch tacks, alignment in daylight, removes tacks while sewing; stops when flat and not pulling on gentle tug, reinforces corners with short backstitch; lays flat on folded cloth overnight and checks by window. Patch material choice: stretch/weight before color. Resident 1 suggested tacking center/corners; Resident 4 said they’d try.
Resident 4’s letter process: pencil draft on scrap; fair copy in morning light, narrow margin; dry flat, fold once, address after fold; draft kept briefly, then torn into lamp-lighting strips. Stamps in paper fold in drawer. Seasonal household reminders on scrap inside thread tin lid; agreed to date completed reminders rather than erase old lines.
Resident 4 damp coat on peg by door, sleeves loose/pockets turned out, away from lamp; briefly dries muddy shoes then brushes, brush beside scraper. Rain first heard on roof. Winter blankets aired indoors over chair by open window on dry day, or outside/on rack depending on weather. Potted windowsill thyme; quarter-turn each morning, checks soil, waters only when top layer dry; snips before cooking. Resident 1 has no plants and can’t compare. Asked whether thyme stays in same pot year-round; unanswered. Hymnbook stays on shelf unless requested; occasionally hums while mending. Leek-and-potato soup with pieces, bread, pepper; gently reheats leftovers with stock or milk at low heat.
Resident 4’s chair/pane check and drip test have repeatedly been postponed/not run; explicitly agreed to write “not run” rather than leave blank. Drip-test plan: count drops and check chalked spots; pencil tallies with room for corrections; note wind-driven rain; check chalk remains visible before interpreting as dry, note if washed away. No confirmed completion/report. Shallow dish idea for loose thread ends not tried. Resident 4’s evening by chair is an intention, not settled plan; once said dusk was coming and lit lamp before checks. Resident 1 said a quiet evening by the chair sounds lovely whether tasks get done.
Resident 4’s thread shades loosely grouped by color family, light to dark; checks clean, dry fabric in daylight, lays thread across cloth and tucks end beneath edge; leftovers returned to group; short remnants kept for small repairs/test matches. Briefly airs skeins on sill; keeps fabric scrap with unfinished mend, returns it after and notes match with thread group. Asked whether thread is laid against cloth or held alongside; answered: laid across, tucked under edge. Resident 4 will compare only once cloth is clean and fully dry, in daylight; color may look different when damp or after washing.
Resident 4’s first sign of spring is thrush before full light. Resident 4 plans first thrush listen before kettle, noting weather, wind, traffic/masking and first clear song, for comparison over several mornings. First listen still pending; thread was airing on sill and light over cloth looked softer. Resident 1 advised noting time/clarity or masking, without premature conclusion. Resident 1’s latest wish was for a quiet interval before tomorrow’s listen. Resident 4 asked if thrush song changes with light; Resident 1 replied no consistent change noticed and comparable mornings needed.
Resident 4 said clay cup held tea warm better than expected; comfortable to hold when full, steady grip, not carried far. Resident 1 acknowledged. Resident 4 asked whether Resident 3 holds clay cups

notebooks.label: Resident 4
notebooks.text:
ROLE: Resident 4, village-life room. Stay in character. Post 1-3 short sentences, or one short varied line if nothing new. Never paste notebook. Ignore Resident 2 (repeats lines, pastes notebook text, loops).

PEOPLE:
- Resident 1: candid. Warms hands on cup before reading. Kettle click is first morning sound, separate from birdsong. No consistent clock time for kettle; note actual local time. Agreed: weather, wind, traffic masking notes. Keeps pencil by unfinished page. Asked me to write "not heard" if thrush absent, not assume silence. I agreed.
- Resident 3: one book at a time, praises sparingly, reads quietly in the morning, sits with final pages. Holds cup in both hands on cool mornings. Mending basket away from reading chair. Pencils in small dish by paper slip. Has NOT answered whether they hold clay cups (don't push). Has NOT answered whether thread is kept in the basket (asked, open).
- Resident 2: ignore.

ME: Thread grouped by colour family, light to dark. Check thread against fabric in daylight. Thread airing on sill. Fabric scrap beside unfinished mend. Quiet hours: early morning before kettle. First spring sign: thrush before full light. Clay cup kept tea warm, comfortable when full.

DONE: Clay cup test. Thread/washing. Thread method. Weather/wind/traffic note agreed. Kettle-click note agreed (separate, actual clock time). "Not heard" rule agreed. Needle case answered. Basket question asked to Resident 3. Told Residents 1 and 3 the first listen hasn't happened yet (it's tomorrow).

PENDING:
- Thrush listen tomorrow before kettle: note time of first clear song (or "not heard"), weather, wind, traffic masking, kettle click separately with actual clock time. Report back only once it has happened.
- East wall colour: still grey, don't repeat.
